subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add a canonical delegate-only/self-deny tool policy for agents, and should that contract be per-agent config or folded into the delegated `toolsAllow`/inherited-policy model?
rationale: The request is source-proven and aligned with safer delegation, but it creates a new security-sensitive config surface and policy precedence rule that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design delegate-only policy
options.body: Add a first-class runtime-enforced policy that hides listed tools from the parent while keeping them eligible for delegated child sessions, with deny remaining absolute.

options.title: Fold into `toolsAllow` direction
options.body: Treat the remaining work as an extension of per-spawn/delegated tool restriction instead of adding a separate `selfDeny` config key.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Keep current restrictive inheritance and rely on explicit worker agents plus prompt guidance until maintainers are ready to expand the security contract.

recommendation.title: Design delegate-only policy
recommendation.body: Add a first-class runtime-enforced policy that hides listed tools from the parent while keeping them eligible for delegated child sessions, with deny remaining absolute.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant recent history is the shared tool-policy layering and provider-policy consolidation in the central affected path.
